title: Piprahwa stupa and relic caskets
summary: At Piprahwa in Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh, W. C. Peppé opened a brick stupa in 1898 and found an inscribed casket linked to the Sakya clan and relics of the Buddha. Archaeological Survey of India digs in 1971–77 found two more caskets. Some scholars identify the site with ancient Kapilavastu, and the dating of the deposit is debated.

uncertainty.note: The National Museum gives the relics as c. 4th-5th centuries BCE; the inscription is dated 240–200 BCE in a reading reported by Tricycle; scholars disagree on whether the two are the same deposit.

as_recorded.value: Holy Buddha Relics, c. 4th 5th centuries BCE

where.modern_name: Piprahwa, Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh, India
where.historical_name: Stupa and monasteries at Piprahwa, identified by some with Kapilavastu of the Sakyas

importance.justification: The caskets are among the earliest claimed Buddha relics and bear a very early Brahmi inscription, tied to the identification of Kapilavastu.

sources.title: Exposition of the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha (National Museum, New Delhi exhibition text)
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

sources.title: Piprahwa Buddha Relics Returned to India: Selling The Buddha

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: the museum says 4th-5th century BCE for the relics while the inscription is reported as 240–200 BCE; the Kapilavastu identification is also contested.
